name: Reading for Devotion (Piety and Application)

objectives.text: Identify one thing a Bible story shows about who God is, such as His love and care
Tell one thing God wants His people to do after hearing a Bible story
Explain that the Bible is God speaking to His people and why Christians pray before reading it
Apply a specific command from Scripture to a situation at school or home
Compose a short prayer of thanks or praise in class that uses words from a passage just read
Explain how a passage directs readers to love God and love their neighbor
Summarize what a passage reveals about God's character and describe a fitting response such as worship, trust, or obedience
Distinguish commands, promises, warnings, and examples in a passage as different ways the text calls for application
Pray through a Psalm in a guided class exercise by turning its praise, confession, and petition into prayer
Explain from Jesus' own words why devotional reading looks for Christ as the center of Scripture's message
Describe the practices the Westminster Larger Catechism gives for reading Scripture with profit, including reverence, attention, application, and prayer
Explain the Reformed teaching that the Holy Spirit illumines readers and uses the Word to sanctify God's people
Apply the truths and promises of a passage to common struggles such as fear, doubt, or temptation
Distinguish moralism from gospel-motivated obedience by comparing two applications of the same passage
Analyze whether a devotional application is faithful to a passage's context or reads a foreign meaning into it
Evaluate sample decisions and case studies in light of specific scriptural principles drawn from their original context
Construct a prayer shaped by the language and theology of a passage read
Produce a written devotional reflection that explains a passage in context and applies its theology to daily life
Defend from Scripture the Reformed view that reading the Bible aims at knowing God and obeying Him and not merely gaining information
Evaluate devotional books and resources for faithfulness to Scripture and sound doctrine

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (God's character, applying commands, love of God and neighbor, Psalm-based prayer, the Spirit's work through the Word, moralism versus gospel fruit, text-shaped prayer, devotional writing, reading for knowing God). Dropped or recast objectives aimed at inner experience: 'express thanks' became composing a prayer in class, 'analyze own heart responses' was removed, personal struggles became applying passages to common struggles, and evaluating personal choices became evaluating case studies. Removed verse copying because it overlaps with memorization. Added recognizing kinds of application, Christ-centered reading, the Larger Catechism's practices for profitable reading, checking applications against their context, and evaluating devotional resources. Added verse anchors and confessional anchors such as WSC Q3, Q89, Q90, and Q99, WLC Q157, WCF 1.6, 1.9, 1.10, and 16.2, and HC Q86.
